title: Critical percolation torus results with the sharp threshold dimension $d_0=6$
statement: For critical Bernoulli bond percolation on the $d$-dimensional torus $T_r^d=(\mathbb Z/r\mathbb Z)^d$, the conclusions of Theorems 1–3, namely the estimates (1)–(4) for the sizes, diameters, and mixing times of the largest finitely many clusters, are expected to hold with $d_0=6$; equivalently, they should hold for every $d>6$. The report notes that this remains beyond the stated lace-expansion method. The corresponding conclusions are proved for a sufficiently spread-out version of the model.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/38](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4081), page 32. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Efficient filtering and smoothing of noisy voltage signals on dendritic trees
statement: Construct an efficient filter for optimal filtering and smoothing of noisy voltage signals on dendritic trees. The state is the vector of voltages at all compartments, with realistic models having approximately $N=10^4$ degrees of freedom; standard Kalman filtering requires $O(N^3)$ time and $O(N^2)$ space. The filter should exploit the tree structure of the cable equation, low-SNR voltage observations, and observations of only a few compartments (fewer than about $100$ at a time).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/39](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4082), page 37. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Monotonicity of the expected volume of a random simplex in dimension 3
statement:
Determine whether, for every pair of 3-dimensional convex bodies $K,L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ with $K\subseteq L$, one has
\[
\mathbb{E}_{X_0,\ldots,X_3\in K}\!\left[\operatorname{vol}\operatorname{conv}(X_0,\ldots,X_3)\right]
\le
\mathbb{E}_{X_0,\ldots,X_3\in L}\!\left[\operatorname{vol}\operatorname{conv}(X_0,\ldots,X_3)\right].
\]
Here the $X_i$ are random points from the indicated convex body, as in the report.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4136), page 17. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Characterization of finite-dimensional versions of random variables
statement: Let $X=(X_1,\\ldots,X_n)$ be an $n$-dimensional version of a random variable $Y$ if there is a function $\\gamma:\mathbb{R}^n\\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $\\gamma(a)>0$ for every $a\\ne0$ and, for every $a\\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the random variables $\\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i$ and $\\gamma(a)Y$ are identically distributed. Characterize all $n$-dimensional versions and, in particular, determine all functions $\\gamma$ that can occur as the standard of an $n$-dimensional version.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4136), page 26. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Extension theorem for differential forms on log canonical pairs
statement: Let $X$ be a normal complex algebraic variety of dimension $n$ and let $\Delta\subset X$ be a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with coefficients in $[0,1]\cap\mathbb{Q}$. Assume that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical. Let $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ be a log resolution, and set $\widetilde\Delta$ to be the largest reduced divisor contained in $\operatorname{supp}\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{non\mbox{-}klt\ locus})$, where the non-klt locus is the smallest closed subset $W\subset X$ such that $(X,\Delta)$ is klt away from $W$. Then, for every integer $p$ with $1\le p\le n$, the sheaf $\pi_*\Omega^p_{\widetilde X}(\log\widetilde\Delta)$ is reflexive.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/02](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4197), page 18. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Weighted Disjoint $S$-Paths Problem for Tree-Distance Weights
statement:
Given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$, a terminal set $S\subseteq V$, and a weight function $w:\binom{S}{2}\to\mathbb{N}$, define
\[
\nu(G,S,w):=\max_{\mathcal P}\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}w\bigl(s(P),t(P)\bigr),
\]
where the maximum is over all sets $\mathcal P$ of node-disjoint $S$-paths, and $s(P),t(P)$ are the ends of $P$. The report states that this optimization problem is solvable in time polynomial in $|V|$ whenever $w$ is representable by tree-distances: there is a tree $T$ such that, for every $s\in S$, a subtree $R(s)$ of $T$ is specified and
\[
w(s,s')=\operatorname{dist}_T\bigl(R(s),R(s')\bigr)\qquad(s,s'\in S).
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/11](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4212), page 42. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Recognizing versal actions
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let $G$ be a linear algebraic group, and let $X$ be an algebraic $k$-variety with a generically free $G$-action. Here generically free means that the stabilizer is trivial on a dense $G$-invariant open subset after passing to an algebraic closure of $k$. The report asks: given such an $X$, how can one determine whether or not the action is versal? A generically free $G$-variety $X$ is versal if, for every generically free $G$-variety $Z$ and every dense $G$-invariant open subset $U\subset X$, there exists a $G$-equivariant map $Z\to U$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/19](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4332), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Limit distribution of Frobenius numbers
statement: The report states the following theorem. Let $d\ge 3$, let $\widehat{\mathbb Z}_{\ge 2}^{d}=\{a=(a_1,\ldots,a_d)\in\mathbb Z^d:\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_d)=1,\ a_i\ge 2\}$, and let $F(a)$ be the largest integer not representable as $m\cdot a$ with $m\in\mathbb Z_{\\ge 0}^{d}$. There exists a continuous non-increasing function $\Psi_d:\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge 0}$ with $\Psi_d(0)=1$ such that, for every bounded set $D\subset\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{d}$ whose boundary has Lebesgue measure zero and every $R\ge 0$, $$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T^d}\#\left\{a\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}_{\ge 2}^{d}\cap TD:\frac{F(a)}{(a_1\cdots a_d)^{1/(d-1)}}>R\right\}=\frac{\operatorname{vol}(D)}{\zeta(d)}\,\Psi_d(R).$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/29](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4410), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Existence and uniqueness of minimal blow-up solutions for inhomogeneous mass-critical NLS
statement:
For the two-dimensional equation
\[
i\partial_tu=-\Delta u-k(x)|u|^2u,
\qquad (t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2,
\]
with smooth positive bounded \(k\), normalized by \(\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}k(x)=1\), and with \(k\in C^5\cap W^{1,\infty}\), let \(Q\) be the positive radial solution of \(\Delta Q-Q+Q^3=0\). Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^2\) satisfying \(k(x_0)=1\) and \(\nabla^2k(x_0)<0\), determine whether, for every \(E_0\) satisfying
\[
E_0+\frac18\int_{\mathbb R^2}\nabla^2k(x_0)(y,y)Q^4(y)\,dy>0,
\]
there exists a time \(t_0<0\) and a unique, up to phase shift, solution \(u\in C([t_0,0),H^1(\mathbb R^2))\) with \(\|u\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}\), energy \(E(u)=E_0\), and blow-up at \(t=0\) concentrating at \(x_0\) in the sense that \(|u(t)|^2\rightharpoonup \|Q\|_{L^2}^2\delta_{x=x_0}\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/41](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4429), page 6. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Jet-spannedness of toric vector bundles from Seshadri-type positivity
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth, complete $d$-dimensional toric variety and let $E$ be a toric vector bundle on $X$. For each invariant curve $C$ through a fixed point, write
\[
E|_C\simeq \mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(a_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(a_r),
\]
and define $\tau(E)$ as the minimum of the integers $a_i$ over all invariant curves and all fixed points of $X$. The report conjectures that, for every integer $k\ge 1$, the condition
\[
\tau(E)\ge k
\]
implies that $E$ is $k$-jet spanned; equivalently, the evaluation map
\[
H^0(X,E)\longrightarrow H^0\!\left(X,E\otimes\mathcal O_X/\mathfrak m_x^{k+1}\right)
\]
is surjective for every point $x\in X$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4527), page 29. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Simultaneous capacity, queue-size, and computational efficiency for switched-network scheduling
statement: Is it possible, for an arbitrary scheduling set (or conflict graph) in the switched-network model, to construct an implementation that is (i) capacity achieving, (ii) has queue sizes that scale polynomially in the number of queues $N$, and (iii) has computational complexity polynomial in $N$? The report states that Shah, Tse, and Tsitsiklis established that the answer is no for arbitrary $G$, assuming the standard computational hypothesis.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/48](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4530), page 50. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: The classical Plateau Problem
statement:
Let $\triangle$ be the unit disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a map $\alpha:\triangle\to\mathbb{R}^n$, define its area by
\[
A(\alpha)=\int_{\triangle}\sqrt{\left|\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x}\right|^2\left|\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial y}\right|^2-\left(\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial x}\cdot\frac{\partial\alpha}{\partial y}\right)^2}\,dx\,dy.
\]
Given a Jordan curve $\Upsilon$, let
\[
F=\left\{\alpha:\triangle\to\mathbb{R}^n:\ \alpha\in W^{1,2}(\triangle)\cap C^0(\triangle),\quad \alpha|_{\partial\triangle}:\partial\triangle\to\Upsilon\text{ is a homeomorphism}\right\}.
\]
Find $\alpha^*\in F$ such that $A(\alpha^*)\leq A(\alpha)$ for every $\alpha\in F$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4535), page 13. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Eckhoff’s conjecture for Radon numbers
statement:
A convexity space on a ground set $X$ is a family $\\mathcal{F}\\subseteq 2^X$ containing $\\varnothing$ and $X$ and closed under intersections. For $P\\subseteq X$, let $\\operatorname{conv}_{\\mathcal{F}} P$ be the intersection of all members of $\\mathcal{F}$ containing $P$. The $k$-th Radon number $r_k$ is the minimum natural number, if it exists, such that every set $P\\subseteq X$ with at least $r_k$ points admits a partition $P=P_1\\cup\\cdots\\cup P_k$ whose convex hulls have a common element. Eckhoff’s conjecture asserts that, in every convexity space with finite $r_2$, one has
\[
r_k\\le (k-1)(r_2-1)+1
\]
for every $k$. The report states that this conjecture is false: for each $k\\ge 3$ there is a convexity space with $r_2=4$ but $r_k\\ge 3(k-1)+2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 70. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Small sets with exponentially high influence
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function whose expectation is around $1/2$; in fact, it is enough that the expectation be bounded away from both $0$ and $1$. For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, set the variables $x_j$ with $j\notin S$ independently and uniformly to $0$ or $1$. The influence of $S$ on $f$ is the probability that this partial assignment does not determine the value of $f$. Is it true that, under the same conditions, there is a set $S$ with $|S|\le n/3$ and influence at least $1-c^n$ for some absolute constant $c$ with $0<c<1$?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 71. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: χ-boundedness of wheel-free graphs
statement: For a graph $G$, let $\omega(G)$ be the size of its largest clique and let $\chi(G)$ be its chromatic number. A wheel in $G$ is a pair $(C,v)$ such that $C$ is an induced cycle of length at least $4$ and $v\in V(G)\setminus V(C)$ has at least three neighbors in $V(C)$. Let $\mathcal C$ be the class of graphs containing no wheel. Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that $\chi(G)\le f(\omega(G))$ for every $G\in\mathcal C$?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 71. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Bárány–Larman Conjecture for the colored Tverberg problem
statement:
Let $d\ge 1$ and $r\ge 2$ be integers. Define $n(d,r)$ to be the smallest number $n$ such that, for every affine map $f:\Delta^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}^d$ and every partition $\operatorname{vert}(\Delta^{n-1})=C_0\mathbin{\uplus}\cdots\mathbin{\uplus}C_d$ with $|C_i|\ge r$ for every $i\in\{0,\ldots,d\}$, there exist $r$ pairwise disjoint rainbow faces $F_1,\ldots,F_r$ satisfying $|C_i\cap F_j|\le 1$ for all $i\in\{0,\ldots,d\}$ and $j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and
$f(F_1)\cap\cdots\cap f(F_r)\ne\varnothing$.

The conjecture is that $n(d,r)=(d+1)r$ for all $d\ge 1$ and $r\ge 2$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4798), page 11. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Existence of $m_k(P)$ for cover-decomposable planar sets
statement: For every cover-decomposable planar set $P$ and every integer $k\ge 2$, the quantity $m_k(P)$ exists, where $m_k(P)$ is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that every $m$-fold covering of the plane by translates of $P$ can be decomposed into $k$ coverings. Here, $P$ is cover-decomposable if some $m(P)$ exists such that every $m(P)$-fold covering of the plane by translates of $P$ can be decomposed into two coverings.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 55. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: 2-colorability of shift-chain hypergraphs
statement: For $A\subset [n]$, let $a_i$ be the $i$th smallest element of $A$. For two $k$-element sets $A,B\subset [n]$, define $A\le B$ if $a_i\le b_i$ for every $i$. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ on vertex set $[n]$ is a shift-chain if, for every pair of hyperedges $A,B\in\mathcal H$, either $A\le B$ or $B\le A$; such a shift-chain has at most $k(n-k)+1$ hyperedges. The hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is 2-colorable if its vertices can be colored with two colors so that no hyperedge is monochromatic. Is it true that shift-chains are 2-colorable if $k$ is large enough?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 83. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Index problem for the contact hypoelliptic operator $P_\gamma$
statement: Let $X$ be a compact contact manifold without boundary of dimension $2n+1$, with contact form $\theta$. Let $\gamma:X\to\mathbb{C}\setminus\{\ldots,-n-4,-n-2,-n,n,n+2,n+4,\ldots\}$ be a smooth function satisfying $\gamma(x)\notin\{\ldots,-n-4,-n-2,-n,n,n+2,n+4,\ldots\}$ for every $x\in X$. Let $P_\gamma$ be the associated second-order hypoelliptic Fredholm differential operator, which is not elliptic. The index problem is to construct a K-cycle $(M,E,\phi)$ on $X$ such that $\eta(M,E,\phi)=[P_\gamma]\in KK^0(C(X),\mathbb{C})$. The report states that Paul Baum and Erik van Erp constructed such a K-cycle, thereby solving the index problem for $P_\gamma$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11137), page 7. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Kurlberg–Rudnick estimates for quantum unique ergodicity of a Hecke basis
statement:
Let \d4f6 be the Anosov toral automorphism considered in the report, let \d4a2=\mathbb{Z}[\alpha] for its largest eigenvalue \(\alpha\), let \(I\) be the corresponding \(\mathcal O\)-ideal, and let \(A(N)\) be the subgroup defined in the report. If \(\{\phi_j\}_{j=1}^N\) is a Hecke basis, \(n=(n_1,n_2)\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\), and \(\nu=n_1v_1+n_2v_2\), define \(\mu(\nu)\) to be the number of quadruples \((\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3,\beta_4)\in A(N)^4\) satisfying
\[
\nu(\beta_1-\beta_2+\beta_3-\beta_4)\equiv 0\pmod{NI}.
\]
Then the estimates stated as Theorem 1 in the report hold:
\[
\mu(\nu)\ll |n|^{16}N^{2+\varepsilon},
\qquad
N^{1-\varepsilon}\ll |A(N)|\ll N^{1+\varepsilon}.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11447), page 42. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Exact value of the real Grothendieck constant K(1)
statement: Determine the exact value of $K(1)$, where, for each integer $r\ge 1$, $K(r)$ is the smallest constant such that for every real matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $$\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)\le \operatorname{SDP}_\infty(A)\le K(r)\operatorname{SDP}_r(A),$$ with $$\operatorname{SDP}_r(A)=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}\,x_i\cdot y_j:x_i,y_j\in S^{r-1}\right\},$$ $S^{r-1}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^r:x\cdot x=1\}$, and $S^\infty$ the unit sphere of the square-summable sequences. The case $r=\infty$ means that the rank constraint is removed.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11451), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Existence of 0/1 polytopes with exponential extension complexity
statement:
For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a set $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{n}$ such that
\[
\operatorname{xc}(\operatorname{conv}(X))\ge \Omega\!\left(\frac{2^{n/2}}{\sqrt{n\log(2n)}}\right),
\]
where $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ is the minimum number of inequalities needed to describe a polytope $Q$ that can be linearly projected onto $P$. In particular, there exists a family of $0/1$ polytopes with no compact (polynomial-size) extended formulation.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11451), page 51. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Minimal class of singularities preserving the normal-crossings locus
statement:
For reduced algebraic or analytic varieties $X$ over a field of characteristic zero, can one find the smallest class of singularities $S$ such that:

1. $S$ includes all normal-crossings singularities; and
2. for every $X$, there exists a proper birational (respectively, in the analytic setting, bimeromorphic) morphism $\sigma\colon X'\to X$ such that $X'$ has only singularities in $S$, and $\sigma$ is an isomorphism over the normal-crossings locus of $X$?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/56](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11454), page 9. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Uniform empirical-Bayes approximation for Poisson means
statement: For independent observations $Y_i\sim\operatorname{Po}(\lambda_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,p$, estimate $\boldsymbol\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p)$ under average quadratic risk $R(\delta,\boldsymbol\lambda)=E_{\boldsymbol\lambda}[p^{-1}\|\delta-\boldsymbol\lambda\|^2]$. For a prior distribution $G$, let $R(G,\delta)=E_G[R(\Lambda,\delta)]$, let $\delta^G(y)=E(\Lambda\mid Y=y)$ coordinate-wise, and let $B(G)=R(G,\delta^G)=\min_\delta R(G,\delta)$. The stated goal is to construct an estimator $\widetilde\delta$ such that $R(G,\widetilde\delta)-B(G)$ is uniformly small in $G$ as $p\to\infty$, with “small” meaning $o(1)$ or, when possible, a sharper rate.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/14](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11581), page 9. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Bourgain’s negative result for nonperturbative purely absolutely continuous spectrum in two frequencies
statement:
Let $v=v(x_1,x_2)$ be a trigonometric polynomial on $\mathbb{T}^2$ with a nondegenerate local maximum. Fix $x=(x_1,x_2)$. For every $\mathord{\lambda}\ne 0$, there exists a set $\mathcal{\Omega}_2$ of positive measure such that, for every $\mathord{\omega}\in\mathcal{\Omega}_2$, the operator
$$
(H(x)\phi)_n=\u0005mathord{\lambda}v(x+n\omega)\phi_n+\phi_{n-1}+\phi_{n+1},\qquad \phi\in\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}),
$$
has some point spectrum and $\mathop{\mathrm{mes}}(\Sigma_{\mathrm{pp}}(H))>0$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11779), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Erdős–Simonovits conjecture on bipartite Turán numbers
statement:
For a family $\mathcal F$ of bipartite graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal F$ as a subgraph, and let $z(n,\mathcal F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex bipartite graph containing no member of $\mathcal F$. Let $C_k$ be the cycle of length $k$, and let $\mathcal C_k=\{C_\ell:3\le \ell\le k,\ \ell\equiv k\pmod 2\}$. Erdős and Simonovits conjectured that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of bipartite graphs, there exists an odd integer $k$ such that

$$\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal F\cup\mathcal C_k)\sim z(n,\mathcal F),$$

where $f(n)\sim g(n)$ means $\lim_{n\to\infty}f(n)/g(n)=1$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/19](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11781), page 20. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Determine the optimal simultaneous-approximation exponent for successive powers
statement:
For a point $\boldsymbol{\xi}=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$, let $\lambda(\boldsymbol{\xi})$ be the supremum of the real numbers $\lambda\ge 0$ such that, for every sufficiently large real $X>1$, the inequalities
$$
|x_0|\le X,\qquad |x_0\xi_i-x_i|\le X^{-\lambda}\quad(1\le i\le n)
$$
admit a nonzero solution $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$. Determine the optimal value
$$
\lambda_n=\sup\bigl\{\lambda(\xi,\xi^2,\ldots,\xi^n):\xi\in\mathbb{R},\ 1,\xi,\xi^2,\ldots,\xi^n\text{ are linearly independent over }\mathbb{Q}\bigr\}.
$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11784), page 11. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Effective determination of representatives for Thue–Mahler equations over finitely generated domains
statement: Let $A$ be an arbitrary finitely generated domain, and let $F\in A[X,Y]$ be a binary form of degree at least $3$ without multiple factors. Consider the Thue–Mahler equation $F(x,y)\in A^{*}$ in $x,y\in A$. It is known that this equation has finitely many solutions $(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_l,y_l)$ such that every other solution is expressible in the form $u(x_i,y_i)$ with $u\in A^{*}$ and $i\in\{1,\ldots,l\}$. Can one determine such representatives $(x_i,y_i)$ effectively for an arbitrary finitely generated domain $A$?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11784), page 17. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Exceptional units conjecture for algebraic integers
statement:
For a positive integer $d$, let
\[
e(d)=\max\{E_0(\alpha)\mid \alpha\text{ is an algebraic integer of degree }d\text{ over }\mathbb{Q}\},
\]
where, for a nonzero algebraic integer $\alpha$, with $K=\mathbb{Q}(\alpha)$ and ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$, $E_0(\alpha)=0$ if $\alpha-1$ is not a unit in $\mathcal O_K$; otherwise $E_0(\alpha)$ is the largest integer $n$ such that $\alpha^j-1$ is a unit in $\mathcal O_K$ for every $1\le j\le n$. The conjecture is that $e(d)<d$ for every $d\ge 7$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11784), page 29. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Diameter conjecture for connected layer families of multisets
statement: Let $\widetilde f(d,n)$ be the maximum diameter $\ell$ of a connected layer family of $d$-element multisets drawn from an $n$-element set. Thus, the multiset family is partitioned into layers $L_0,\ldots,L_\ell$ such that, for every $i<j<k$, every $v\in L_i$, and every $w\in L_k$, there exists $u\in L_j$ with $u\supseteq v\cap w$ (where inclusion and intersection are interpreted for multisets). Conjecture that $\widetilde f(d,n)=d(n-1)$ for all positive integers $d,n$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/24](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11786), page 37. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Bernhard–Jablan Conjecture on unlinking numbers
statement:
For a link diagram $D$, let $u(D)$ be the minimum number of crossing changes in $D$ required to obtain a diagram representing an unlink, and let $u(L)=\min_D u(D)$ over all diagrams $D$ representing $L$. Define the BJ-unlinking number recursively by $u_{BJ}(D)=0$ if $D$ represents an unlink, and otherwise by
\[
u_{BJ}(D)=1+\min_v u_{BJ}(D_v),
\]
where $D_v$ is obtained by switching a crossing $v$ of $D$, with the minimum taken over minimal diagrams of the resulting link for which the value is already defined; finally, let $u_{BJ}(L)=\min_D u_{BJ}(D)$ over all minimal-crossing-number diagrams $D$ representing $L$. Bernhard and Jablan conjectured that, for every link $L\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, $u(L)=u_{BJ}(L)$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11790), page 24. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Exact recovery of separated point sources by total-variation minimization
statement:
Let $x=\csum_j a_j
ej\delta_{\tau_j}$ be a signal with amplitudes $a_j\in\mathbb{C}$ and locations $\tau_j\in T\subset[0,1]$. Suppose the observed data are the $n=2f_c+1$ low-frequency Fourier coefficients $y=F_nx$, where
$$
y(k)=\cint_0^1 e^{-i2\pi kt}\, x(dt)=\csum_j a_j e^{-i2\pi k\tau_j},\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z},\quad |k|\le f_c,
$$
and let $\lambda_c=1/f_c$. Define
$$
\cDelta(T)=\cinf_{(t,t')\in T,\ t\ne t'} |t-t'|.
$$
If $\cDelta(T)\ge 2\lambda_c$, then solving
$$
\cmin_{\tilde{x}} \c|\tilde{x}\c|_{TV}\quad\ctext{subject to}\quad F_n\tilde{x}=y
$$
recovers $x$ exactly. For a real-valued signal, a minimum distance of $1.87\lambda_c$ suffices.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/29](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11791), page 23. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Dimension-only additive upper bound for hypersurface Laplace eigenvalues
statement:
For a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{m+1}$ with smooth boundary $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$, and for all $k\ge 1$, is it possible to find constants $A_m,B_m$ depending only on the dimension $m$ such that
\[
\lambda_k(\Sigma)\operatorname{Vol}(\Sigma)^{2/m}\le A_m I(\Omega)^{1+2/m}+B_m k^{2/m},
\]
where $I(\Omega)=\operatorname{Vol}(\Sigma)/\operatorname{Vol}(\Omega)^{m/(m+1)}$ is the isoperimetric ratio?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12005), page 24. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Optimal constant in the classical Lieb–Thirring inequality
statement:
Determine the optimal constant $K_d>0$, depending only on the dimension $d$, such that for every $N\in\mathbb{N}$, every collection of functions $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_N\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\psi_j\psi_k\,dx=\delta_{jk}$, and every $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N\in[0,1]$, one has
\[
\sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_j\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|\nabla\psi_j|^2\,dx\ge K_d\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left(\sum_{j=1}^N\lambda_j|\psi_j|^2\right)^{1+2/d}\,dx.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12005), page 43. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Sharp tail decay for continual crossing in dynamical percolation
statement:
For critical dynamical site percolation on the triangular grid, under the rescaled dynamics associated with a quad $Q$ and its left–right crossing event $C_Q$, determine whether the continual-crossing probability in (7) has the upper-tail decay
$$
\mathbb{P}\bigl[\omega_s\in C_Q\ \text{for all }s\in[0,t]\bigr]\le \exp\bigl(-t^{2/3+o(1)}\bigr),\qquad t\to\infty.
$$
The report presents this as a heuristic conjectural bound; it also records only superpolynomial upper bounds and a dynamical-FKG lower bound in (7).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12016), page 15. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Well-posedness of the space-time variational formulation for diffusion on an evolving surface
statement:
For the evolving-surface problem, let $H$, $W:=\{v\in H\mid \dot v\in H'\}$, and $\mathring W:=\{v\in W\mid v(\cdot,0)=0\text{ on }\Gamma_0\}$ be as defined in the report. With $\alpha\in L^\infty(\Gamma^*)$, $\varepsilon>0$, and
\[
a(u,v)=\varepsilon(\nabla_\Gamma u,\nabla_\Gamma v)_0+(\alpha u,v)_0,
\]
the report states that the following problem is well-posed: given $f\in H'$, find $u\in\mathring W$ such that
\[
\langle\dot u,v\rangle+a(u,v)=\langle f,v\rangle\qquad\text{for all }v\in H.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/15](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12343), page 59. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Independence numbers of sparse powers of Kneser graphs
statement:
Let $K_n^t$ be the graph with vertex set
\[
V(K_n^t)=\{(A_1,\ldots,A_t): A_i\subset\{1,2,\ldots,n\},\ |A_i|=n/3\text{ for all }i\},
\]
where two distinct vertices $(A_1,\ldots,A_t)$ and $(B_1,\ldots,B_t)$ are adjacent if and only if there is an index $i$, $1\le i\le t$, such that $A_j=B_j$ for every $j\ne i$ and $A_i\cap B_i=\varnothing$. Let $\alpha(K_n^t)$ denote its maximum independent-set size. Conjecture: for every $\epsilon>0$, there exist $n$ and $t$ such that
\[
\frac{\alpha(K_n^t)}{|V(K_n^t)|}\le \epsilon.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12481), page 31. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Erdős–Fajtlowicz conjecture on chromatic number versus clique subdivisions
statement:
For every integer $n\ge 2$, let $H(n)$ be the maximum of $\chi(G)/\sigma(G)$ over all graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices, where $\chi(G)$ is the chromatic number and $\sigma(G)$ is the largest integer $p$ such that $G$ contains a subdivision of $K_p$. The Erdős–Fajtlowicz conjecture asserts that there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that
\[
H(n)\le C\frac{n^{1/2}}{\log n}.
\]
The report states this conjecture as proved.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12481), page 35. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Numerical analysis of a direct Galerkin discretization of the curl eigenvalue problem
statement:
For a domain $\Omega$ topologically equivalent to a ball $(\beta=0)$, analyze the direct Galerkin discretization of the self-adjoint curl eigenvalue problem with closed traces: find $H_h\in V_h:=W_0^1(\Omega_h)+\operatorname{grad}W_\partial^0(\Omega_h)$ and $\alpha$ such that
\[
\int_\Omega \operatorname{curl}H_h\cdot v_h\,dx
=\alpha\int_\Omega H_h\cdot v_h\,dx
\qquad\text{for all }v_h\in V_h.
\]
Here $W_0^1(\Omega_h)\subset H_0(\operatorname{curl},\Omega)$ is a lowest-order edge-finite-element space on a curvilinear simplicial triangulation of $\Omega$, and $W_\partial^0(\Omega_h)$ is spanned by piecewise-linear nodal basis functions associated with nodes on $\partial\Omega$. The report states that the numerical analysis of this discretization remains open.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/56](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12730), page 37. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Exact characterization of the monomial-convergence set for bounded holomorphic functions on $B_{c_0}$
statement:
Determine the set
\[
\operatorname{mon}H^\infty=\left\{z\in B_{c_0}:\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^{(\mathbb N)}}\left|\frac{\partial^\alpha f(0)}{\alpha!}z^\alpha\right|<\infty\text{ for all }f\in H^\infty(B_{c_0})\right\}.
\]
The report establishes the bounds
\[
\left\{z\in B_{c_0}:\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{j=1}^n(z_j^\star)^2<1\right\}\subseteq\operatorname{mon}H^\infty\subseteq\left\{z\in B_{c_0}:\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{j=1}^n(z_j^\star)^2\le 1\right\},
\]
where $(z_1^\star,z_2^\star,\ldots)$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $z$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12866), page 13. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Optimality of the exponential factor in a polynomial inequality
statement:
For $1\le r\le\infty$, let $\Lambda(N)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}_0^{(\mathbb{N})}:2^{\alpha_1}3^{\alpha_2}5^{\alpha_3}\cdots\le N\}$. Determine whether the exponent in the exponential factor of the estimate
\[
\sup_{z\in B_{\ell_r}}\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda(N)}|c_\alpha z^\alpha|
\le N^{1-\frac{1}{\min\{2,r\}}}e^{-\left(\sqrt{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\min\{2,r\}}\right)+o(1)\right)\sqrt{\log N\,\log\log N}}\sup_{z\in B_{\ell_r}}\left|\sum_{\alpha\in\Lambda(N)}c_\alpha z^\alpha\right|
\]
for arbitrary scalars $(c_\alpha)_\alpha\subset\mathbb{C}$ is optimal; equivalently, determine whether the displayed exponential exponent can be improved. The report states that the exponent of $N$ is optimal but that the optimality of the other exponent remains open.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12866), page 35. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Growth of the averaging length for Dirichlet-polynomial $L^p$ norms
statement:
For a Dirichlet polynomial $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n n^{-s}$ and $1\le p<\infty$, define
\[
\|f\|_p^p:=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(it)|^p\,dt.
\]
For a fixed large $N$ and a constant $C>1$, let $T_p(N,C)$ be the smallest $T$ such that
\[
\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}|f(it)|^p\,dt\le C\|f\|_p^p
\]
for every Dirichlet polynomial $f$ of degree at most $N$. How does $T_p(N,C)$ depend on $p$? In particular, is $T_p(N,C)=O(N)$ when $1\le p<2$? The report remarks that the value of $C>1$ is presumably not important.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12866), page 53. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Classification of D-finiteness for three-dimensional octant-walk generating functions
statement:
For every step set $S\subseteq\{-1,0,1\}^3\setminus\{(0,0,0)\}$, let
\[
a_S(x,y,z,t)=\sum_{n\ge 0}\sum_{i,j,k\ge 0}a_{n,i,j,k}x^iy^jz^kt^n,
\]
where $a_{n,i,j,k}$ is the number of length-$n$ lattice walks that start at $(0,0,0)$, remain in the nonnegative octant $\mathbb{N}^3$, use only steps from $S$, and end at $(i,j,k)$. Determine exactly which step sets $S$ yield a D-finite generating function $a_S(x,y,z,t)$ and which yield a non-D-finite generating function.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12872), page 32. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Degree bounds for rational sum-of-squares multipliers on curves
statement: Given an even degree $2s$, find an integer $k\in\mathbb{N}$ depending only on $s$ and invariants of an irreducible, non-degenerate real projective curve $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ with dense real points, such that for every form $p\in P_{X,2s}$ there exists $q\in\Sigma_{X,2k}$ with $pq\in\Sigma_{X,2s+2k}$. The report answers this question in Theorem 1.2 on the following page by giving an explicit $k$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12975), page 50. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Higher-rank interpolation for sheaves on \(\mathbb{P}^2\)
statement: Let \(\xi\) be the Chern character of positive rank of a stable sheaf on \(\mathbb{P}^2\), and let \(F\in M(\xi)\). A sheaf \(E\) satisfies interpolation with respect to \(F\) if \(H^i(E\otimes F)=0\) for every \(i\). Determine the minimal slope \(\mu\in\mathbb{Q}\), subject to \(\mu+\mu(\xi)\ge 0\), for which there exists a vector bundle \(E\) on \(\mathbb{P}^2\) of slope \(\mu\) satisfying interpolation with respect to \(F\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/31](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13101), page 24. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Grünbaum mass partition problem
statement: Determine the function \(\Delta:\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{N}\) defined by \(\Delta(j,k)\) equal to the smallest dimension \(d\) such that every collection \(M=\{\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_j\}\) of \(j\) mass distributions in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) admits an arrangement \(\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_k\}\) of \(k\) affine hyperplanes that equiparts \(M\). Here, if \(g=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)\in(\mathbb{Z}/2)^k=\{0,1\}^k\), the corresponding orthant is \(O_{\mathcal H}^{g}=H_1^{i_1}\cap\cdots\cap H_k^{i_k}\), and equipartition means that for every \(g\in(\mathbb{Z}/2)^k\) and every \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,j\}\), \(\mu_\ell(O_{\mathcal H}^{g})=2^{-k}\mu_\ell(\mathbb{R}^d)\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/40](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13110), page 10. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Contractibility of the space of convex-position polygon arrangements
statement: We say an arrangement of convex sets is in convex position when the sets are indexed by $1,\ldots,n$ and, for every triple $\{K_i,K_j,K_k\}$, $i<j<k$, each set intersects the boundary of the convex hull of the triple in a single connected component, these components are pairwise disjoint, and the sets appear counter-clockwise around the boundary in order according to their indices $(\cdots i,j,k\cdots)$. Define a metric on pairs of arrangements by taking the maximum of the Hausdorff distances between pairs of sets with the same index. A $k$-gon is a convex polygon with at most $k$ vertices. Is the space of $n$ $k$-gons in convex position, modulo affine transformations, contractible?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/40](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13110), page 55. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Undecidability of the finite development problem for permutoids
statement: Given partial permutations $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ of a finite set $X$ (bijections between subsets of $X$) satisfying: (1) $p_1=\operatorname{id}_X$; and (2) for all $i,j$ with $\operatorname{dom}(p_i)\cap\operatorname{ran}(p_j)\neq\varnothing$, there is at most one $k$ such that $p_k$ extends the partial composition $p_i\cdot p_j$; determine whether there exists a finite set $Y\supseteq X$ and permutations $f_i$ of $Y$ extending $p_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,m$, such that whenever $p_k$ extends $p_i\cdot p_j$, one has $f_i\circ f_j=f_k$. The report states that this decision problem is algorithmically undecidable: no algorithm can decide, for every such input, whether the required finite $Y$ and permutations exist.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13112), page 39. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Polynomial-time solvability of bin packing with a fixed number of item types
statement:
For every fixed constant $d$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm for the one-dimensional cutting-stock/bin-packing problem with $d$ item types: type $i$ has size $s_i\in[0,1]$ and multiplicity $a_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, all input numbers are binary encoded, and the algorithm finds the minimum number of bins of capacity $1$ needed to pack exactly the prescribed multiplicities. Equivalently, with $P=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^d:s^Tx\le1\}$, it computes
$$
\min\left\{\sum_{x\in P}\lambda_x:\sum_{x\in P}\lambda_xx=a,\ \lambda\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^{P}\right\}.
$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2014/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13353), page 17. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Stabilization of nonlinear controllable systems by trigonometric-polynomial feedback
statement:
Assume that the Lie algebra generated by the vector fields satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Lie}_{x=0}\{f_j\mid 1\le j\le m\}=\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Is it possible to construct, for some $N\ge 0$ and $\omega>0$, a time-varying feedback law
\[
u_j=\sum_{k=-N}^{N}v_k^j(x)e^{i\omega kt},\qquad j=1,2,\ldots,m,
\]
such that the trivial solution of the closed-loop driftless system
\[
\dot{x}=\sum_{j=1}^{m}u_jf_j(x),\qquad x\in D\subset\mathbb{R}^n,\quad u\in\mathbb{R}^m,\quad m<n,
\]
is asymptotically stable? Here the functions $v_k^j(x)$ are piecewise smooth, satisfy $v_k^j(x)=v_{-k}^j(x)$ for all $x\in D$, and obey $v_k^j(x)\to0$ as $x\to0$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13497), page 57. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
